title: Theoretical Characterization of Absolute Correlation
summary: The fixed-mask estimate falls below the experimental absolute correlation, while the theoretical explanation of multiple-mask and modular-addition effects remains unresolved.

formal_statement.body: Develop a detailed theoretical characterization of absolute correlation in settings where the theoretical estimate fixes the linear masks $\lambda^{(0)}$ and $\lambda^{(1)}$, while multiple linear masks may contribute in a manner analogous to the conventional linear-hull effect. In particular, explain how this multiple-mask effect interacts with consecutive modular addition and why substantially higher absolute correlation is expected. This problem is motivated by the partition-based differential-linear attack on Chaskey, where the experimental absolute correlation is $2^{-7.37}$ rather than the fixed-mask theoretical estimate $2^{-7.958}$; account for this observed gap in terms of the multiple-mask and modular-addition effects.

scope.domain: Differential-linear cryptanalysis of ARX ciphers, focusing on absolute correlation and linear-hull effects.
parameters: linear masks lambda^(0) and lambda^(1), fixed in the theoretical estimate
multiple linear masks, possible contributors analogous to the conventional linear-hull effect
consecutive modular addition, the operation associated with substantially higher absolute correlation
experimental absolute correlation 2 raised to -7.37 and fixed-mask theoretical estimate 2 raised to -7.958, the observed and baseline values
scope.unresolved_remainder: A detailed theoretical characterization remains unresolved: explain how multiple-mask contributions interact with consecutive modular addition, why substantially higher absolute correlation is expected, and the observed gap between the experimental and fixed-mask estimates.

citations.label: Improved Differential-Linear Attacks with Applications to ARX Ciphers

progress.summary: The paper notes that its theoretical estimate fixes two masks, while multiple masks may contribute as in the conventional linear-hull effect and consecutive modular addition may increase absolute correlation. It then explicitly leaves the detailed theoretical understanding as an open question.
citation_labels: Christof Beierle et al., Improved Differential-Linear Attacks with Applications to ARX Ciphers
